explanation: Transpose across the main diagonal, then reverse each row. Together these transformations move every original cell to its clockwise-rotated position, using the existing matrix.
attribution: Original C# implementation written for EPI Practice from the displayed contract; no upstream reference code copied.
correctness: Transposition maps original position (r,c) to (c,r). Reversing every row then maps that position to (c,n−1−r), exactly the coordinate rule for a 90-degree clockwise rotation. Both transformations use the existing rows.
walkthrough: Transpose [[1,3],[5,7]] to [[1,5],[3,7]], then reverse each row. The result is [[5,1],[7,3]].
edgeCases: No replacement rows or second matrix are needed.
